summary: The first RNG divergence is caused by the skipped read.c:unpunish() call, not by later monster-turn behavior. For a punished, non-confused hero, seffect_remove_curse() calls unpunish(), which deletes the chain through delobj(); delobj_core() reaches obj_resists() and consumes rn2(100) even though an ordinary iron chain has 0% resistance. read.js currently records note_unported("read.c unpunish") at this branch.

source.branch: Whole-function scope is read.c:unpunish() (3064-3077), reached from seffect_remove_curse() when Punished is true and Confusion is false. In this recording, the hero is punished by the prior wished-for uncursed punishment scroll before reading a blessed remove-curse scroll. unpunish() clears W_CHAIN, deletes the saved chain, then clears W_BALL; the deletion path has observable RNG and object/map state effects.
callers: C: read.c:doread() calls seffects() at 635; read.c:seffects() dispatches SCR_REMOVE_CURSE and SPE_REMOVE_CURSE to seffect_remove_curse() at 2225-2227; read.c:seffect_remove_curse() calls unpunish() only under Punished && !confused at 1598-1599.

JavaScript: cmd.js:runReadCommand() -> read.js:doread() -> read.js:seffects() -> read.js:seffect_remove_curse(). The SCR_REMOVE_CURSE branch dispatches at read.js:3358-3360, but read.js:2028-2032 calls note_unported() instead of unpunish(). A private analogue in js/bury.js:209 is reached only from bury_an_obj() at 268.
dependencies: read.c:unpunish() calls worn.c:setworn(NULL, W_CHAIN), then delobj(savechain), then setworn(NULL, W_BALL) (read.c:3068-3076). setworn() clears the chain and ball worn masks and the corresponding hero pointers; preserve this order and its state effects.

invent.c:delobj() (1428-1433) calls delobj_core(obj, FALSE); delobj_core() (1435-1462) calls zap.c:obj_resists(obj, 0, 0) before object extraction, floor redraw, and obfree(). These are side effects of the void call and cannot be omitted merely because its return is unused.

zap.c:obj_resists() (1458-1472) returns early only for the Amulet, invocation objects, and Rider corpses. For an ordinary iron chain it calls rn2(100) unconditionally, even with zero resistance chances. JavaScript counterparts exist in js/invent.js:delobj()/delobj_core() and js/bury.js:obj_resists().

evidence: The saved scan .cache/synthetic-scans/v15/wizard-blessed-remove-curse-unpunishes-hero.json identifies the first mismatch at zero-based step 86, RNG index 2929: C has rn2(100)=45 at zap.c:1469 while JavaScript has rn2(5)=0 at monmove.c:538. Its unported list names read.c unpunish. This establishes that the next C draw is missing before JavaScript reaches the later monster movement draw; the zap.c annotation names the draw helper, not the earlier source owner.

The immutable recording challenges/cases/v15/wizard-blessed-remove-curse-unpunishes-hero.session.json reaches step 86 on the confirmation space after wishing for an uncursed scroll of punishment and a blessed scroll of remove curse. The C RNG log for step 86 starts with rn2(100)=45 @ obj_resists(zap.c:1469), followed by distfleeck() and monster-turn draws.

In the frozen source at commit 6d2c675aad59f170ec44980d6afce47f08ae7423, read.c:seffect_remove_curse() (1489-1605) executes its Punished && !confused branch at 1598-1599. The complete target function read.c:unpunish() (3064-3077) saves uchain, clears W_CHAIN, calls delobj(savechain), and only then clears W_BALL. This is the source behavior that the read path must reach; the source function scope is the whole unpunish(), not an isolated RNG insertion.

The first C draw follows the call chain read.c:unpunish() -> invent.c:delobj() -> invent.c:delobj_core(FALSE) -> zap.c:obj_resists(). delobj_core() tests obj_resists() at invent.c:1444-1446; obj_resists() draws rn2(100) at zap.c:1469 for ordinary objects. A punishment chain is not one of the protected object types, so the 0% chance comparison still consumes the recorded draw.

The examined JavaScript read.js:seffect_remove_curse() reaches state.uball && !confused and records note_unported("read.c unpunish") at 2028-2032, so it skips chain deletion as well as clearing the ball slot. js/bury.js has a private helper named unpunish() at 206-229 that preserves the obj_resists() draw, but its only caller is bury_an_obj() at 267-269; the remove-curse caller does not reach it. Treat this as the read.c unpunish source-function port and caller wiring, retaining its full W_CHAIN -> delobj -> W_BALL order and shared object-slot state.
